A tooltip, a modal and toasts beside the top layer

Three ideas from the element catalogue. A native tooltip, a modal dialog and a popover are painted by the page in the top layer, upright and outside any canvas, so a canvas can't draw them. Each demo takes one of them and does the part a canvas can do: it draws its own tooltip from the title text, it draws the scene behind a modal dialog moving away, and it draws toasts that are dialogs kept out of the top layer.

Toast stack in the scene

Press Save a few times. Each toast is a non-modal <dialog open> that the canvas draws sliding in and stacking. Undo and the cross on a toast are real buttons.

    A dialog opened with the open attribute or show() stays in normal layout, so it can be a drawable child and the canvas can animate it. Opened with showModal(), or as a popover, it would be in the top layer and the canvas couldn't draw it.

    How it works

    An element's picture holds what the element paints in normal flow. The top layer is a separate list that the browser paints over the whole page: modal dialogs, popovers, and the picker of a customisable select. A native title tooltip is drawn by the browser's own interface, outside the page. None of these can be passed to drawElementImage(). The three demos work beside that limit in three ways:

    • Replace it. The tooltip is an ordinary element with role="tooltip", drawn by the canvas where the term was drawn. getClientRects() of an inline element returns its drawn boxes, also when the draw was rotated.
    • Draw the other half. The modal dialog stays in the top layer. The canvas draws what is behind it.
    • Keep it out of the top layer. A dialog with the open attribute isn't in the top layer. It needs position: static to be laid out inside the canvas.

    A fourth idea from the same list, a menu that opens flat from buttons drawn in perspective, is already built as /popovers/: there the popover stays in the top layer and CSS anchor positioning keeps it on the drawn button.

    Live checks

    The checks wait for a tap. Each one builds its own small canvas in a corner of the window, and none of them touches the demos above. No check opens a modal dialog, because that moves focus.

    Findings

    Measured in headless Chromium 157 on 2026-11-21, with a mouse, a keyboard and emulated touch. Not yet run on a phone.

    • A canvas can draw its own tooltip at the drawn place of a term. getClientRects() of an inline element inside a rotated draw returned a box whose middle was 0.1 px from where the rotation puts it. The box is the bounding box of the rotated text: 42.4 by 29.5 px for a 39 by 19 px span.
    • The drawn tooltip opens by mouse, by tap and by keyboard focus. pointerover, click and focusin reach the terms where they are drawn. The page moves each title to data-tip, so the browser's own tooltip doesn't appear as well, and points the term at the tooltip element with aria-describedby.
    • An open popover isn't in the picture of the element that holds it. None of 50 sampled pixels of the drawn box had the popover's colour. The same holds for a modal dialog (measured on /elements/).
    • While a dialog is modal, the scene in the canvas is still drawn and can't be hit. elementFromPoint() at the drawn scene returned the dialog. With closedby="any" a tap on the drawn scene closed the dialog. After it closed, a checkbox in the scene took a tap again.
    • The canvas can stand in for ::backdrop for its own scene. It draws the scene at 84% size through blur(), saturate() and brightness() filters from dialog.open, and the toggle and close events of the dialog ask for the paint. A filter on a draw doesn't change where the element is found.
    • A <dialog open> is drawn as a drawable child if it is position: static. Its buttons are found where it is drawn, also while it slides. A dialog added while the page runs is drawn from the next paint.
    • Not verified: everything on a phone. In particular a long press on a term (Android may show its own menu), the on-screen keyboard over the toast form, and where Android centres the modal dialog while the keyboard is open. A screen reader on the tooltip and on the toasts wasn't tried.
